newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed after election.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed after election.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Tuesday after Canada's ruling Liberal government won just a narrow majority in Monday's federal election.
Dealers said the market had been expected to rally if the Liberals won a convincing majority, but the market was trading sideways on their failure to do so.

"The books were relatively long looking for a pop after the election, didn't get it, so now we're going to back slightly into our regular supply for the week," said one T-bill dealer at a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.0 percent from 3.01 percent at the close of trading on Monday.
The governing Liberals won 155 of the 301 seats in Canada's Parliament in yesterday's elections, giving them a majority of just four seats.

With the election providing little reason for T-bills to rally, the money market's focus has now shifted to the weekly auction of T-bills. The Bank of Canada this afternoon will auction C$4.4 billion of three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.33 percent from 3.34 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.75 percent from 3.77 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded near 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
